messages:
chris: Heads-up — enterprise customer is asking for BYOK with HSM-backed keys + per-tenant KMS and stricter RBAC for key usage. They want proof we never have plaintext key material and an incident playbook if key access is suspected. Can we map custody boundaries and compliance requirements before the CT?

liz: Agree. High-level: envelope encryption + customer-managed root keys in their HSM/KMS. Redwood should hold only wrapped data keys or ephemeral session tokens. No plaintext KMs in control plane.

alex: For runtime: we need to confirm what operations must occur in our serving path. If we can restrict to KMS:Encrypt/Decrypt or Sign/Verify calls (no key export) we can avoid handling raw key material. Any reason we need raw unwrapped keys in memory?

liz: Ideally no. Options: 1) Remote unwrap inside customer KMS (GenerateDataKey without plaintext), 2) Use HSM to perform unwrap/sign and return ciphertext payloads or ephemeral DEKs, 3) If unwrapping must occur, do it inside a constrained, audited enclave (short-lived, minimal privileges).

maya: From compliance POV: customers will ask for: strong RBAC (separation of duties), immutable audit logs for key usage (who/what/when/action), configurable retention (some regs want 7+ years but varies), and legal proof of key destruction. Also make sure location of logs meets residency claims (GDPR concerns).

kevin: Vulnerability triage angle: define fast rotation & revocation flows. If we detect suspicious KMS credentials or HSM compromise, we need automated revocation hooks and failover keys ready. Also record reproducible forensic snapshots (WORM copies of logs) before rotation.

chris: Can we list the RBAC roles we should define for a BYOK customer? I was thinking: key-admin (customer), key-usage-service (Redwood runtime role with kms:Decrypt/kms:GenerateDataKey), key-audit-reader (security), and key-recovery (emergency ops). Thoughts?

liz: That map makes sense. Important: require MFA/wallet/approval for key-admin ops (rotate/delete). Enforce just-in-time elevation for recovery roles. Note: limit the runtime role to only the minimal allowed API calls, and scope by ARN to the customer key.

alex: Example IAM policy snippet for usage role (customer-managed AWS KMS):
```json
{
  "Version": "2012-10-17",
  "Statement": [{
    "Effect": "Allow",
    "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey","kms:Encrypt","kms:ReEncrypt*"],
    "Resource": "arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:123456789012:key/abcd-..."
  }]
}
```
This should be scoped to exact key ARNs and condition on encryption context where possible.

maya: Audit log granularity request from compliance: must capture API call, principal identity (service account + origin IP/region), encryption context, request parameters (no plaintext), result code, and a monotonic event id. Logs should be exportable and signed.

kevin: Incident playbook draft (short):
1) Detect & isolate: revoke runtime role tokens, shift traffic to fallback key.
2) Preserve evidence: snapshot KMS/HSM audit logs to immutable storage.
3) Rotate keys: perform key rotation and rewrap data keys; push new key ARN to config.
4) Notify customers + legal if scope crosses PII boundaries.
5) Postmortem: timeline + mitigation & KT.
We need automation for steps 1-3.

chris: For fallback key, are we expecting to host a Redwood-managed fallback? Customer might object, but we need emergency runway. Maybe require customer opt-in for fallback with a signed SLA clause.

liz: Exactly — fallback only if customer explicitly enables and signs off. Otherwise service degradation until customer provides new key. This is a policy decision (legal + sales).

kevin: Also consider split-key model for extreme custody boundaries: customer holds master key, Redwood holds a blinding key. Unwrap requires both. That reduces single-point compromise risk but is operationally heavier.

alex: Implementation questions: 1) Do we support Azure Key Vault & GCP KMS HSM variants? 2) How do we handle cross-region latency for KMS calls on hot paths? Maybe local cache of wrapped DEKs with short TTL and strict audit.

liz: Support should include AWS CloudHSM/AWS KMS (BYOK), Azure Key Vault HSM, GCP External Key Manager. Documented constraints: latency SLO impacts, and customers with stringent latency needs should deploy Redwood Dedicated in their VPC with local KMS adjacency.

maya: Legal also requires proofs for key deletion (metadata of delete counters, API receipts). We should capture these and expose via audit exports per customer.

chris: Question: who owns the design doc + PR for RBAC and playbook? Propose @liz author, @alex runtime design, @maya compliance sign-off, @kevin triage/playbook. Meeting next Wed AM for review.

liz: I can take initial draft. Will push to design repo and ping here.

sre-bot: Created ticket SEC-2026 BYOK-HSM-RBAC (https://redwood/ticket/SEC-2026) and added assignees: liz, alex, maya, kevin. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: Scheduled design review meeting: 2026-03-25 10:00 PT. Calendar invites sent.

chris: Thanks — please add a short checklist to the ticket: required audit fields, RBAC roles, rotation playbook, fallback policy, supported KMS vendors, and performance constraints.

liz: Will do. Adding checklist now. :+1:
